title: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Kings 15](/bible/1-kings/15)

**[1 Kings 15:1-5](/bible/1-kings/15#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/15#v1)</sup> Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat reigned Abijam over Judah.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/15#v2)</sup> Three years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/15#v3)</sup> And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as the heart of David his father.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/15#v4)</sup> Nevertheless for David’s sake did the Lord his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem:
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-kings/15#v5)</sup> Because David did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

- Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem and walks in all the sins of his father, his heart not perfect with the Most High as David's was.
- The children did what they saw their fathers do, not merely what was said, which is why the Most High teaches His people to be different.
- Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented.
  - **[Psalm 51:1-3](/bible/psalms/51#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/51#v1)</sup> Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/51#v2)</sup> Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/51#v3)</sup> For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.

    David's repentance after Nathan came to him: he pleads for mercy and acknowledges his transgression.

**[1 Kings 15:6-15](/bible/1-kings/15#v6)**
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-kings/15#v6)</sup> And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-kings/15#v7)</sup> Now the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-kings/15#v8)</sup> And Abijam slept with his fathers; and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-kings/15#v9)</sup> And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned Asa over Judah.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-kings/15#v10)</sup> And forty and one years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-kings/15#v11)</sup> And Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord, as did David his father.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-kings/15#v12)</sup> And he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-kings/15#v13)</sup> And also Maachah his mother, even her he removed from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove; and Asa destroyed her idol, and burnt it by the brook Kidron.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-kings/15#v14)</sup> But the high places were not removed: nevertheless Asa’s heart was perfect with the Lord all his days.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-kings/15#v15)</sup> And he brought in the things which his father had dedicated, and the things which himself had dedicated, into the house of the Lord, silver, and gold, and vessels.

- After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did.
- Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron.
- Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

**[1 Kings 15:16-24](/bible/1-kings/15#v16)**
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-kings/15#v16)</sup> And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-kings/15#v17)</sup> And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-kings/15#v18)</sup> Then Asa took all the silver and the gold that were left in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants: and king Asa sent them to Ben–hadad, the son of Tabrimon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-kings/15#v19)</sup> There is a league between me and thee, and between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold; come and break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-kings/15#v20)</sup> So Ben–hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of the hosts which he had against the cities of Israel, and smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel–beth–maachah, and all Cinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-kings/15#v21)</sup> And it came to pass, when Baasha heard thereof, that he left off building of Ramah, and dwelt in Tirzah.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-kings/15#v22)</sup> Then king Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah; none was exempted: and they took away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-kings/15#v23)</sup> The rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Nevertheless in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-kings/15#v24)</sup> And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.

- There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa.
- Asa takes silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's house and sends it to Benhadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha, and Benhadad smites cities of Israel so Baasha stops building Ramah.
- Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

**[1 Kings 15:25-32](/bible/1-kings/15#v25)**
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-kings/15#v25)</sup> And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned over Israel two years.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/1-kings/15#v26)</sup> And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/1-kings/15#v27)</sup> And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel laid siege to Gibbethon.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-kings/15#v28)</sup> Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-kings/15#v29)</sup> And it came to pass, when he reigned, that he smote all the house of Jeroboam; he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him, according unto the saying of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite:
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/1-kings/15#v30)</sup> Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/1-kings/15#v31)</sup> Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/1-kings/15#v32)</sup> And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

- Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father.
- Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite.
- This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.

**[1 Kings 15:33-34](/bible/1-kings/15#v33)**
> <sup>[33](/bible/1-kings/15#v33)</sup> In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasha the son of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty and four years.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/1-kings/15#v34)</sup> And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.

- Baasha reigns twenty-four years in Tirzah and does evil, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin by which he made Israel to sin.
- The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.
